name: Ramesh Chauhan
profile: Indian beverage entrepreneur (b. 1940) of the Parle family. Parle bought the Bisleri brand from an Italian entrepreneur in 1969 and he built it into India's dominant bottled-water brand; he also created Thums Up, Limca, Gold Spot and Maaza, sold to Coca-Cola in 1993. After talks to sell Bisleri to Tata Consumer ended in 2023, daughter Jayanti (Vice Chairperson) and CEO Angelo George run it.
interesting_fact: After Coca-Cola left India in 1977 he launched Thums Up and built it into India's leading cola; Coca-Cola later bought Parle's soft-drink brands (Thums Up, Limca, Gold Spot, Maaza, Citra) in 1993.
deep_cut_fact: Known as 'RJC' to friends, he holds a double major in mechanical engineering and business management from MIT, returned home at 22, and introduced bottled mineral water to India at 27. His 2013 biography 'Thunder Unbottled, From Thums Up to Bisleri' was written by friend and ex-Newsweek UN bureau chief Patricia J Sethi.

name: Ajei Gopal
current_role: President & CEO, Procore Technologies (since Nov 10, 2025); director of Synopsys and Fiserv
profile: Indian-American software executive (IIT Bombay BTech, Cornell PhD in computer science). As CEO of Ansys 2017-2025 he grew the simulation-software maker and led it into its ~$35B acquisition by Synopsys, joining Synopsys' board. Earlier: Silver Lake operating partner, Symantec CTO, and CA/HP roles. In 2025 he succeeded founder Tooey Courtemanche as CEO of construction-software firm Procore.

notes: Public-company CEO; route via Procore communications. Relevant to data-center angle: Procore software is used on large construction projects. Ansys bio: https://ansys.com/company-information/leadership/dr-ajei-s-gopal

name: George Kurian
current_role: CEO, NetApp (since June 2015); Director, The Cigna Group
profile: Indian-born tech executive (Princeton electrical engineering, Stanford MBA) who worked at Oracle, McKinsey, Akamai and Cisco, where he ran the Application Networking and Switching Technology Group, before joining NetApp in 2011.
